title: HarborBridge Dedicated Capacity Discovery
header: 2026-03-04 15:00 PST | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (CTO), Lisa Chen (Head of Infra), Tom Avery (SRE), Nina Patel (PM)
summary: Discovery focused on Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for HarborBridge: requirements for isolation, burst capacity for peak trading windows, scaling expectations, SLAs, and security controls (VPC, KMS, SSO). Customer requested pricing ranges, SOC2 and compliance docs, and a short benchmarking pilot. Technical follow-up to scope network/VPC peering and pilot test plan.
topics: Reserved GPU sizing and burst strategy
Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
transcript:
00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Alex, AE on Redwood. Priya and Diego from our solutions team are here to cover the technicals. Mark: hey hi, thanks. I'll hand off to Lisa to set context.
00:16 Lisa: Yep, thanks. We're evaluating Dedicated reserved capacity for inference across a few models — customer support triage and fraud detection first, then trading assistant later. Big things for us are latency under 120ms p50 for the triage path, absolute data isolation, and the ability to burst during end-of-month statement processing.
00:34 Priya: got it. when you say burst, do you mean short-lived spikes where you add GPUs, or more of a scheduled daily/weekly increase?
00:42 Lisa: Both. We have scheduled nightly jobs and unpredictable spikes during incidents. Ideally reserved baseline capacity plus a burst pool we can use on-demand.
00:50 Diego: Redwood Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools with configurable burst capacity options. you can reserve X GPUs for steady state and allow burst to a larger pool; bursts are subject to region capacity but we do offer burst guarantees for enterprise contracts.
01:06 Mark: what's the typical lead time for guaranteed burst? our infra team needs to know procurement timing.
01:11 Alex: depends on region and contract. with Dedicated we can price and commit burst pools as part of the reserved contract — that gives you predictable capacity and SLAs. standard lead times are a few weeks for capacity planning but we can provision uncommitted burst faster if available.
01:26 Tom: on isolation — does Dedicated mean our models, traffic, and KV cache are single-tenant? we can't have co-tenancy for certain PII workloads.
01:34 Priya: yes, Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and compute. for VPC-private deployments we can also do private control plane or on-prem if you need air gap. KV cache (prefix cache) sits in the same tenant; we don't share caches across customers.
01:49 Nina: curious about encryption; keys managed by us?
01:52 Diego: we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. you can bring-your-own KMS and we support envelope encryption for data-at-rest.
02:01 Mark: ok. what about model updates and rollouts — we need canarying so a bad model doesn't propagate.
02:06 Priya: our rollout tooling supports canary and A/B deploys, automatic fallback to previous model variant on errors, and route policies based on latency or capacity. you can pin routes to a model version for stability.
02:20 Lisa: performance — any recommended quantization or model families to hit the latency goals? we'll mostly run Llama-family open models and a couple smaller instruction-tuned models.
02:29 Priya: depends on seq length and prompt patterns. for short assistant style prompts we recommend int8 or 4-bit quant variants; Redwood Optimize can profile and recommend quantization/ batching settings. batching and prefix caching help throughput without hurting p50 too much.
02:44 Tom: what's the expected cold-start behavior for KV cache? during burst are we losing cache or it's shared?
02:50 Diego: cache is per-dedicated pool. if you scale horizontally into new nodes they'll warm the cache; that's why we suggest a warm-up plan in the pilot — pre-load typical prompts or use background warming to reduce tail latency.
03:02 Mark: SLA questions — uptime and latency SLOs?
03:06 Alex: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime targets and latency SLAs in enterprise contracts. for pricing/commit levels we can offer tighter latency SLOs and increased priority routing.
03:16 Nina: vendor lock-in: if we want to move models or change infra later, how portable is the setup?
03:21 Priya: API surface is consistent across Hosted and Dedicated. model artifacts are standard formats (PyTorch/ggml/etc) and we offer export tooling for customer-owned models; network config like VPC peering will be specific but not lock-in for model formats.
03:34 Lisa: regulatory — we operate in multiple regions, need data residency. can Dedicated be regional?
03:39 Diego: yes, you can pin capacity to a region and restrict routing. for stricter needs we do private deployments with a customer-managed control plane.
03:49 Tom: any compliance docs we can see? SOC2, penetration tests, ISO?
03:53 Alex: yes, we'll share SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. I'll add that to next steps.
03:58 Mark: cost — rough ballpark for reserved GPU pricing? we need to compare to self-hosted infra costs.
04:03 Alex: for a ballpark, reserved capacity with 8x A100-equivalent GPUs a month runs in the mid-five-figure range depending on commitment length and burst included; exact quote we'll send. Many customers find total cost-of-ownership lower once you factor ops and inference engineering.
04:20 Lisa: can you do host-level metrics and per-token cost breakdowns? our finance team will want that for forecasting.
04:26 Priya: Console shows token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, and latency breakdowns. we also emit traces and exportable CSVs for cost modeling.
04:36 Tom: networking — we plan to peer our VPC. is there support for private peering and restricted egress?
04:41 Diego: yes, we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and limited egress rules for private deployments. firewall and peering config will be in the onboarding runbook.
04:52 Nina: pilot idea — can we do a 2-week bench with a subset of traffic to validate latency and cost?
04:56 Alex: absolutely. typical pilot: 2-4 weeks, bench two models, synthetic traffic + a small production shadowing run. we'll provide a pilot runbook and help with benchmarks.
05:06 Mark: downtime risk during model swap, any best practices?
05:10 Priya: use rolling deploys with canary traffic, automatic fallback, and pre-warming. Redwood can handle zero-downtime model swaps for stateless flows — for heavy KV-dependant flows pre-warm is recommended.
05:24 Tom: monitoring and alerts integration — we use PagerDuty and Datadog.
05:28 Diego: we integrate with Datadog, Prometheus, and send webhook alerts; can forward audit logs and trace ids to your systems.
05:37 Lisa: any concerns about co-tenancy noise in noisy-neighbor situations?
05:41 Priya: Dedicated is single-tenant compute so noisy neighbor should be eliminated; for Hosted multi-tenant we do noisy neighbor mitigation but not full isolation.
05:51 Mark: what about model quant degradation — if we quantize to 4-bit do we get hallucination spikes?
05:56 Priya: sometimes; Redwood Optimize will run quality regressions tied to prompt sets and alerts on regressions. you can set guardrails to fallback to higher-precision variants for certain routes.
06:09 Alex: are there any blockers on your side for a pilot? pricing, legal, infra access?
06:14 Mark: legal will want SOC2 and DPAs, procurement needs ballpark pricing, and infra needs checklists for VPC peering. once those are in place we can run pilot.
06:25 Nina: timeline — we have an internal Q2 plan; want pilot in next 6 weeks ideally.
06:30 Alex: sounds doable. we'll aim to send pricing and security docs this week and schedule an infra deep-dive with Tom and Lisa next week.
06:40 Diego: technical note — for burst guarantees we need to align on region and instance family. we'll include recommended instance families based on your models in the proposal.
06:51 Priya: also recommend a warm-up plan for KV and sample prompts for Optimize to profile batching/quantization.
06:59 Mark: question on logs retention — we have retention policies, can we control retention per environment?
07:03 Priya: yes, retention is configurable; enterprise plans have longer retention and export options.
07:12 Tom: last technical — what's the max throughput per node? we want to size for peaks of ~1200 rps for small prompts.
07:18 Diego: depends on model and quant; 8x-A100-equivalent can handle roughly X rps for small seq lengths with batching; we'll run sizing in the pilot and provide concrete numbers.
07:30 Nina: ok. recap and next steps?
07:33 Alex: recap: we'll send SOC2 and security docs, a preliminary pricing + capacity recommendation, pilot runbook, and schedule an infra call next week.
07:43 Mark: thanks. Lisa: thanks all.
07:46 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.
07:49 [call ends]
